ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure has a carbonyl structure, where the central carbonyl carbon forms a double bond with the upper oxygen atom and is connected on the right to R1; the left side of the carbonyl carbon is connected to an α-carbon, and this α-carbon is connected to R on the left and H below. There is also a B: species at the lower left that is not connected to the organic skeleton. The figure has curved arrows from B: to H, from the C-H bond region toward the carbonyl direction, and near the carbonyl oxygen, but the problem requires ignoring the arrows. Reasoning: After ignoring the arrows, the organic skeleton is R-CH-C(=O)-R1. Representing both R and R1 with the wildcard atom * gives the connection relationship *-C-C(=O)-*, which can be written as *CC(*)=O. B: is an independent component, separated with a dot, and represented as [B]. Therefore, the overall SMILES is *CC(*)=O.[B].

method.method_draft: First describe the structural skeleton visible in the image, ignoring all curved arrows as instructed: R-CH-C(=O)-R1 plus a disconnected B: species. Convert R and R1 to wildcard atoms, encode the alpha carbon and carbonyl carbon connectivity in SMILES, then append the separate boron/base component after a dot to obtain *CC(*)=O.[B].

planner_metadata.image_role: Read the image as showing an alpha carbon bearing R and H bonded to a carbonyl carbon; the carbonyl carbon is double-bonded to O and single-bonded to R1. A separate base label B: is drawn nearby, and curved arrows are present but must be ignored.

planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use SMILES conventions: replace unspecified substituents R and R1 with wildcard atoms '*', omit the explicitly drawn hydrogen because it is implicit on carbon, write the ketone fragment as *CC(*)=O, and represent the disconnected base species as a separate component [B] joined by a dot.
